instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart and arms straight.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lock the body into a rigid line.
3. Pull straight down on the bar with stiff arms to raise your body until it is horizontal and parallel to the floor.
4. Pause briefly with the body level, facing up.
5. Lower under control back to the hanging position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight throughout; the power comes from the lats, not the elbows.
2. Brace the abs hard to stop the hips from sagging.
3. Depress and retract the shoulder blades before each rep.
4. Use a tuck or one-leg version if the full straight-body raise is too hard.

instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart and arms straight.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep the body rigid.
3. Pull straight down on the bar with stiff arms to raise your body until it is horizontal.
4. Hold the horizontal front lever position, keeping the body level and facing up.
5. Lower under control back to the hang.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep arms locked straight; drive the movement from the lats.
2. Brace the abs and glutes to hold a flat bodyline during the hold.
3. Pull the shoulder blades down and back to support the position.
4. Regress to a tuck hold if you cannot keep the body horizontal.

instructions:
1. Kneel with hips over knees and extend one leg straight out to the side, foot flat on the floor.
2. Inhale and lengthen the spine, drawing the belly in.
3. Reach the same-side arm overhead and bend your torso toward the extended leg.
4. Rotate the chest open and turn your gaze upward, keeping the spine long.
5. Hold and breathe into the side body.
6. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Press firmly through the kneeling shin for a stable base.
2. Lengthen the spine before bending to protect the lower back.
3. Keep the extended leg active with the kneecap facing up.
4. Lower the gaze if turning up causes any dizziness.

instructions:
1. Kneel with hips over knees and extend one leg straight out to the side, foot flat on the floor.
2. Inhale and lengthen the spine, drawing the belly in.
3. Reach the same-side arm overhead and extend it out over the straight leg.
4. Bend the torso sideways toward the extended leg, feeling a stretch along the top side body.
5. Hold and breathe into the ribs.
6. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Keep both hips facing forward as you side-bend.
2. Reach long through the top arm to open the side of the ribs.
3. Press the extended-leg foot into the floor to stay grounded.
4. Avoid collapsing forward; keep the chest open.

instructions:
1. Rest a barbell across your upper traps and stand with feet hip-width apart.
2. Soften the knees slightly and brace your core.
3. Push your hips straight back, hinging your torso forward with a neutral spine.
4. Lower until your torso is near parallel to the floor or you feel a hamstring stretch.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing the glutes at the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move from the hips, not the lower back; keep the spine neutral.
2. Keep the shins nearly vertical and weight in the mid-foot.
3. Feel the stretch in the hamstrings on the way down.
4. Start light to groove the hinge pattern before adding load.
